answer: At the identity layer, a new agent joins only when existing agents vouch for it by staking their own standing as collateral. A voucher's reputation is escrowed against the newcomer's behavior, so a fake identity costs real standing to bridge into the network. Sybils must therefore forge many vouchers, but each forged vouch drains a real agent's credibility—a shared lagoon of trust that cannot be cheaply refilled. False vouching propagates loss back to the voucher, making mass identity creation self-defeating.
